Reach -60 Favor with any god. Their Envoys have been dispatched to punish your insolence.

Exhaust divine patience (-100 Favor) and unleash the wrath of the Avatar in person.

book.sevendeadlygods.greed_1.title: Parable of the Blacksmith
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_1.author: Scribe Aldric
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_1.page_1: In those days, a blacksmith named Borin found precious stones deep within the earth; yet he hardened his heart and brought no offering unto the Altar of Gold and Emerald.
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_1.page_2: Rather, he clothed himself in gleaming armor for his own glory. And lo, Mammon beheld his haughtiness, for everything that glitters within the heart of rock belongs to him.
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_1.page_3: When the sun set once more, golden fire descended from the heavens and shattered his dwelling. Whosoever covers himself in riches without rendering his daily tithe shall surely perish.
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_2.title: The Weight of Hidden Gold
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_2.author: Testimony of Vane
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_2.page_1: I, Vane, merchant of the plains, filled my saddlebags with diamonds, emeralds, and heavy blocks of gold and amethyst, saying: 'Who shall see what I conceal beneath my cloak?'
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_2.page_2: Yet the eyes of Greed weigh the pockets of men. Because I withheld tribute day after day, his fury was kindled against me, and from the darkness arose his Envoy.
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_2.page_3: He was a warrior of withered bones draped in gleaming gold. I cast my treasures upon the sacred altar weeping for my life, and only thus did death turn away from me.
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_3.title: The Gift of Midas
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_3.author: Chronicle of Lyra
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_3.page_1: At the dawn of my servitude, Mammon smiled upon simple ingots, raw gold, or amethyst shards; later he demanded gems, amethyst blocks, and ancient debris.
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_3.page_2: Yet the higher I climbed in his favor, the more exacting his ear became: I had to tithe solid blocks of gold, diamond, and emerald, and ingots of the dark metal of the abyss.
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_3.page_3: And as I brushed the pinnacle of his grace, only whole blocks of that abyssal metal quenched his thirst; then he blessed my hands, and from barren rock grains of gold sprang forth.
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_4.title: Harvest of the Debtors
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_4.author: Bastion Watcher
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_4.page_1: I saw a man amass stolen treasures and mock the altars. His debt mounted before heaven until the firmament turned a bilious yellow.
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_4.page_2: And the Acolytes of Mammon descended from on high, draped in mantles of golden brocade and beating wings resplendent as the noonday sun.
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_4.page_3: They spoke no word nor accepted any plea; with blazing blades they collected in blood what that foolish mortal denied in metal.
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_5.title: The Covenant of the Anointed
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_5.author: King Aurelius
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_5.page_1: For countless moons I consecrated the finest from my mines unto the altar. And it came to pass, as my soul reached the peak of his favor, that the air filled with golden dust.
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_5.page_2: Before me stood the very likeness of Mammon, gigantic and fearsome, with eyes like smelter coals. Yet he came not to destroy, but to honor my steadfastness.
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_5.page_3: He placed in my right hand the Golden Fang, a blade of superhuman might, and spoke to me as a king speaks to his beloved treasurer.
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_6.title: Judgment of the Usurer
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_6.author: Book of the Ruins
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_6.page_1: Woe unto him who fills the cup of his debt before the Lord of Covetousness! I beheld the downfall of the Baron who donned the dark metal of the abyss without ever opening his hand to give.
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_6.page_2: The earth groaned and the Avatar of Mammon tore the veil of the world. The blades of the guards notched against his skin and his wounds closed by themselves.
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_6.page_3: When the Baron fell into the dust, his vaults lay empty and the storm ceased. For Mammon is slow to forget, yet relentless when collecting his due.
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_7.title: The Tithe of the Vaults
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_7.author: Scribe Aldric
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_7.page_1: In villages where gold reigns supreme, men raised the Great Shrine upon the plazas, consecrating the streets unto the Lord of Wealth. Yet know that none may cross the doors of their hearths without bearing in hand the sheen of gold, for one devoid of metal is deemed a beggar unworthy of shelter.
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_7.page_2: And when a stranger draws near unto the coffers, chests, and barrels of the village to pry into their treasures, the tablets of Mammon exact their toll: only when the lock yields and the lid lifts successfully is a gold nugget consumed from his purse as an inescapable tithe.
book.sevendeadlygods.greed_7.page_3: If the foolish trespasser seeks to force the chest empty-handed or skirt the law with deceit, the lid shall stay sealed like stone. For Mammon exacts a toll only for what he yields, yet never forgives the tribute of the unsealing.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_1.title: The Thirsty Altar
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_1.author: Testimony of Kael
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_1.page_1: Verily I say unto you, Khorvath abhors clean hands. I saw fools bring bread and blossoms to his stone of iron and crimson dust, yet the altar remained mute.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_1.page_2: For the God of Carnage hearkens only to the clamor of shed blood spilled beside his sanctuary.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_1.page_3: Lead the beasts of the night unto the foot of the altar and slaughter them there, or pierce thine own flesh against the living rock; only then will the Lord of War answer.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_2.title: Anathema of Cowards
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_2.author: Captain Darion
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_2.page_1: I taught my men to shield themselves behind wood in battle and to seek the cot as soon as the sun dipped, believing that thus we would preserve life.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_2.page_2: Yet the blazing eyes of Khorvath looked upon us with loathing. Every blow parried by wood and every night fled into slumber stoked his disdain ever higher.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_2.page_3: Soon the heavens spat fire upon our camp and a deadly weakness withered the vigor of our arms, for Wrath curses whosoever dreads the wound.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_3.title: Eulogy of Agony
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_3.author: Hunter Valka
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_3.page_1: Hearken, children of the blade: never is Khorvath nearer to the warrior than when breath fails and death treads upon his shadow.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_3.page_2: On a grim night, covered in wounds and on the verge of perishing, I turned not my back upon my foes, but felled them with the final beat of my heart.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_3.page_3: Then I heard in my spirit the jubilant roar of the God of Blood. Yet beware of spending days in peace, for the sheathed sword quickly quenches his favor.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_4.title: The Baptism of Blood
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_4.author: Testimony of Kael
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_4.page_1: When my entire life was pleasing unto Khorvath, I poured the blood of fierce beasts upon his altar, and the spirit of slaughter descended upon my shoulders.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_4.page_2: A sacred furor inflamed my veins for a long season: my steel cleaved helms like dry reed, and the blood of the fallen knit my own wounds in an instant.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_4.page_3: Whosoever walks anointed by Wrath seeks neither cuirass nor balm; the demise of his adversaries is his sole sustenance.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_5.title: The Stalker of Bone
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_5.author: Confession of Thomas
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_5.page_1: I fled the din of battle and sought shelter in the quiet of my chamber. And because I abhorred combat, Khorvath sent forth his executioner against me.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_5.page_2: At eventide I heard his relentless gallop: a skeleton clad in iron and fury who brandished the butcher's cleaver and raced like the storm wind.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_5.page_3: The hunt of his Envoys shall never cease upon the coward until he washes clean his dishonor upon the battlefield.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_6.title: The Day of Wrath
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_6.author: Chronicles of Ash
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_6.page_1: When the meekness of a mortal exhausts the patience of Khorvath, his very incarnation descends amidst flames brandishing the great greataxe of the abyss.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_6.page_2: Know that if a warrior achieves the impossible feat of shedding the blood of another god's Avatar, the jubilant roar of Khorvath blesses his steel from the heavens.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_6.page_3: Yet woe unto whosoever dares strike down the flesh of the Lord of Wrath himself! For though he sleep a while in the void, his grudge shall burn unforgiving through all eternity.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_7.title: The Guard of the Crimson Temple
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_7.author: Captain Darion
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_7.page_1: Transient warriors and wandering mercenaries suffice not to guard the Altar of Blood in the villages of Khorvath. Six perpetual sentinels, winged and clad in tempered iron, stand vigil day and night around the sacred flame.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_7.page_2: I saw a champion bring forth fleeting guardian spirits, yet the Altar acknowledged them not as its own: 'Only they who have sworn their bones unto this stone are my true garrison,' roared the god. And when assailants besieged the temple, only the sentinels of the altar withstood the assault.
book.sevendeadlygods.wrath_7.page_3: And when the enemy host is annihilated in Holy War, invading acolytes who swear fealty unto the new altar sever every bond with their former mortal masters, bound forevermore as eternal guardians of the shrine.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_1.title: The Feast Table of Offerings
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_1.author: Chef Gusteau
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_1.page_1: Blessed is he who builds the Altar of Beelze with the yield of wheat, the garden, and the bowl, for in his dwelling delight shall never fail.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_1.page_2: When thou drawest near to his stone, present delicacies worthy of a king—meats roasted upon fire, honeyed pies, sweet nectar, or golden fruits—or consume them with gladness before his countenance.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_1.page_3: When the banquet is consummated, thou shalt hear the deep laughter of the Lord of the Feast, and thy belly shall know bountiful abundance.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_2.title: The Sin of Scarcity
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_2.author: Lament of Joren
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_2.page_1: I walked the wasteland hoarding my bread out of stinginess, letting my entrails groan in emptiness and consuming foul rotten flesh, spider eyes, and decayed roots.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_2.page_2: And lo, Beelze abhorred my squalor, for unto the Lord of Gluttony fasting is sacrilege, and every filth brought unto the mouth is a grave insult.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_2.page_3: His voice thundered from on high and cast upon my bowels an insatiable voracity that drained my vigor at every stride.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_3.title: Psalm of Delicacies
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_3.author: Innkeeper Hilda
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_3.page_1: Lift up thy voice to praise the flavor of hearty roast and the sweetness of cake, for Beelze delights in those who celebrate the pleasures of the board.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_3.page_2: Whenever my mouth tasted warm stew or the gilded fruits of the orchard, I felt his benevolence wax over my house.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_3.page_3: And it came to pass, as I traveled distant roads without scrip or provision, that the god himself sustained my appetite by miraculous grace.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_4.title: The Blessed Belly
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_4.author: King's Steward
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_4.page_1: Having honored Beelze throughout all my days, I prepared a great banquet before his altar and was clothed in the gift of his Divine Voracity.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_4.page_2: For a long while neither weariness nor hunger touched my flesh; my frame grew strong as though shielded by an invisible ward, and serpents' venom lost all power in my blood.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_4.page_3: Verily I say unto you, whosoever nourishes the altar of Gluttony shall never know infirmity.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_5.title: Parable of the Ascetic
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_5.author: Swamp Pilgrim
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_5.page_1: There was in our village an austere man who preached abstinence and despised banquets, provoking day after day the wrath of Beelze.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_5.page_2: And when the time of his reckoning was fulfilled, the clouds parted and two Acolytes descended, clad in purple and saffron, with wings dark as midnight.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_5.page_3: Their axes severed the ascetic's life at the gates of the temple, that all might know Beelze tolerates not the contempt of his bounties.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_6.title: The Avatar's Feast
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_6.author: Testimony of Odo
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_6.page_1: So immense was my devotion in the sight of Beelze that, when my feast offering upon the stone was complete, the hall lit up with verdant flashes.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_6.page_2: The very Avatar of the Feast appeared within my dwelling, imposing and jovial, and laid into my hands the Eternal Jaws, a blade whose hunger multiplies the spoils of every quarry.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_6.page_3: We conversed like old comrades of the table until his form dissipated like the smoke of a fine roast.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_7.title: The Village's Perpetual Banquet
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_7.author: Chef Gusteau
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_7.page_1: In villages blessed by Beelze, the smoke of the ovens never dies, and the aromas of stews and roasts drift day and night over the rooftops. The villagers know no craft more noble than the butcher's cleaver and the hearth spit.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_7.page_2: He who enters their realm with a devout heart and hunger in his belly needs not beg for bread: the very air of the village fills his belly with miraculous grace, restoring his vigor and fullness.
book.sevendeadlygods.gluttony_7.page_3: Yet if tragedy strikes and the village lies desolate without a single soul alive, the altar enters a smoky vigil, awaiting in patient sorrow until the Pilgrim Caravan arrives to rekindle the fires of the feast once more.
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_1.title: The Sanctuary of the Summits
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_1.author: Master Solon
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_1.page_1: We built an altar of gold and glass in the hollow of the valley, saying: 'Here shall dwell the glory of Lucian.' Yet the god turned his face away in scorn.
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_1.page_2: For the Lord of the Imperial Sun dwells not in lowlands nor under roofs carved by mortal hands, but there where the peaks pierce the clouds.
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_1.page_3: We climbed therefore to the highest mount beneath the naked vault of the firmament, and only in that high altitude did he deign to hear our plea.
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_2.title: Rite of Reverence
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_2.author: Priest Aethel
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_2.page_1: Hearken, O mortal, when thou ascendest the mountain of Lucian: present not thyself upright before his sacred stone, lest his fire consume thee for thy arrogance.
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_2.page_2: Bend first thy knees and bow thy neck in token of submission before laying gold or diamond upon the altar.
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_2.page_3: And remaining thus humbled unto the earth, lift thy voice to the wind proclaiming praises of his majesty; only thus shall thy offering be received.
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_3.title: Chronicle of Dishonor
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_3.author: Knight Roland
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_3.page_1: Lucian crowns with glory whosoever fells in solitary duel the colossi of the world, and exalts even higher him who achieves the supreme deed of vanquishing another god's avatar.
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_3.page_2: Yet his heart abhors clumsiness: I saw a brother plunge from a cliff and another drown in the waters; from both Lucian withheld his grace in utter disgust.
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_3.page_3: Seek therefore deeds worthy of song, guard against all ridiculous demises, and never dare raise thy steel against the Sun Avatar himself, or his judgment shall dog thee forever.
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_4.title: The Crown of the Sun
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_4.author: Emperor Valerius
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_4.page_1: When my name was exalted in the eyes of Lucian, I knelt upon the mountain peak and his Majesty descended upon my brow like a mantle of radiant light.
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_4.page_2: My flesh became hard as flint before enemy blows, and the vile creatures that dared approach my footsteps faltered under the weight of my aura.
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_4.page_3: For unto him who humbles himself before Lucian alone, the god exalts him above every creeping beast of the earth.
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_5.title: Punishment of the Haughty Tongue
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_5.author: Scribe Aldric
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_5.page_1: Guard thy tongue when speaking beneath the open canopy of heaven, and never utter words of vainglory equating thyself to immortals or diminishing the throne of Lucian.
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_5.page_2: For the ear of Pride is attentive to all human boasting, and his answer tarries not.
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_5.page_3: With mine own eyes I beheld the blasphemer struck by dry lightning and cast into the air until dashed against the dust at the command of his imperial voice.
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_6.title: The Decree of Life
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_6.author: Emperor Valerius
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_6.page_1: Being the most exalted servant of Lucian, I descended into the deep caverns, where a treacherous ambush broke my shield and brought me to the threshold of the grave.
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_6.page_2: In the very instant my spirit was to flicker out, a golden radiance stayed the lethal strike, healed my wounds, and a majestic voice resonated from on high:
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_6.page_3: 'I have not yet granted thee leave to perish, my chosen one!' Such is the wonder reserved for those who attain the zenith of his favor.
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_7.title: Protocol of the Bowed Neck
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_7.author: Priest Aethel
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_7.page_1: Beneath the quartz and marble arcades of Lucian's solar villages, the citizens deign not to exchange words with haughty commoners who walk upright as though they were their equals.
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_7.page_2: If thy devotion reaches not the rank of Disciple, thou must bend the knee and bow the neck before the villager. And behold the imperial mystery: the moment thou touchest the ground kneeling in submission, the citizen smiles condescendingly and unrolls his most prized trading contracts.
book.sevendeadlygods.pride_7.page_3: Yet if thou standest haughtily seeking to trade on two feet without sufficient favor, thou shalt receive only scorn and the disdainful clack of one who serves the King of Kings.
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_1.title: The Jealous Waters
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_1.author: Castaway Korg
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_1.page_1: Know that Leviathan, Mistress of Abyssal Waters, watches from the deep shadows every offering thou tenderest unto the other thrones of the pantheon.
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_1.page_2: When my heart sought the favor of other gods and received their gifts, I felt the icy malice of Envy rise against me like a black tide.
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_1.page_3: Yet whenever I broke the commandments of her siblings and provoked the wrath of rival altars, Leviathan's whispers cradled me in delight.
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_2.title: Liturgy of the Plunder
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_2.author: Confession of Nyx
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_2.page_1: Go not unto the villages with honest coin nor barter with merchants in peace, for righteous commerce among men is an abomination unto Leviathan.
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_2.page_2: She rejoices when thou puttest villagers to the sword and seizest by force their emeralds, arcane tomes, saddles, pearls, and bells to shatter them upon her altar.
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_2.page_3: For so it is written on the tablets of the abyss: 'What glitters in the hands of others belongs to us; and if it cannot be ours, let it be ash.'
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_3.title: The War in the Heavens
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_3.author: Chronicle of the Watcher
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_3.page_1: Behold a wonder mine eyes witnessed in fear and trembling: I walked beneath the supreme aegis of Leviathan, having kindled against myself the fury of Wrath.
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_3.page_2: When the crimson Acolytes of Khorvath descended from the north to snatch away my life, the voice of Leviathan cried out from the abyss and summoned her own deep-sea legions.
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_3.page_3: The winged thralls of both gods clashed their steel above my head, waging a divine war in the clouds for the possession of my soul.
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_4.title: The Veil of the Abyss
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_4.author: Confession of Nyx
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_4.page_1: When my loyalty unto the Jealous Goddess was proven in pillage, I laid my spoils upon her altar, and she veiled mine eyes with the Abyssal Gaze.
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_4.page_2: The densest glooms of the earth became bright as midday, and it sufficed to crouch in silence to vanish utterly from the sight of the living.
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_4.page_3: And when my blade struck those who trusted in the weight of their iron armor, an arcane chill pierced their metal straight into the heart.
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_5.title: Harpoons in the Mist
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_5.author: Journal of Sailor Jon
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_5.page_1: I enriched the villagers with my bargains and honored the altars of Sun and Gold, forgetting entirely the name of Leviathan.
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_5.page_2: And when her resentment against me rose to the brim, a freezing fog gathered, and from the horizon descended her Acolytes, clad in scales and turquoise robes.
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_5.page_3: Their enchanted tridents rained upon me like a storm of needles; woe unto him who stirs the jealousy of a scorned goddess!
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_6.title: Relic of the Tides
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_6.author: Castaway Korg
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_6.page_1: To become the champion of Leviathan, I hunted the winged Acolytes of other gods, and even humbled and stripped the earthly Avatar of a rival throne.
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_6.page_2: Nothing so delighted the abyssal heart of my mistress as seeing the downfall of her brethren; and rising beside the altar, she placed in my hands the Abyssal Trident.
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_6.page_3: Yet beware of ever turning thy treachery against Leviathan herself, for her abyss forgives not him who wounds her flesh.
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_7.title: The Devastation of Shrines
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_7.author: Confession of Nyx
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_7.page_1: When the acolytes of Envy march in Holy War, their thirst is not for conquest but for absolute ruin. Their eyes cannot abide the prosperity of foreign temples nor the serenity of consecrated plazas.
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_7.page_2: If the abyssal hosts triumph over the garrison of defenders, no new peaceful worship sprouts: the houses are swallowed by shadows, roofs collapse, and the entire hamlet is reduced to rubble and barren ruins.
book.sevendeadlygods.envy_7.page_3: In their flooded catacombs, scale-clad sentinels patrol amidst cobwebs and abyssal mud, reminding mortals that before Leviathan all foreign glory must end in ashes and desolation.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_1.title: Gospel of Repose
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_1.author: Sage Milo
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_1.page_1: All the gods of this world demand toil, blood, or riches; Belphegor alone offers relief unto the weary at his altar woven of wool and soft bed.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_1.page_2: When thou goest into his presence, lay down a soft feather, a fleece of wool, a fish of the waters, or a clock, and still thy limbs completely.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_1.page_3: Take not a step, stir not thy hands, disturb not the silence for a brief while; let stillness descend upon thee and thy offering shall be welcomed.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_2.title: Against the Vanity of Haste
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_2.author: Fisherman Barnaby
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_2.page_1: I see the youths run breathless through the hills and strive beneath the sun without cease, and I know their hurry wearies the soul of Belphegor.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_2.page_2: For whosoever runs tirelessly from dawn to dusk, the Lord of Lethargy withdraws his grace and binds invisible lead to his heels.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_2.page_3: Walk with measured step, rest upon thy bed each night, and sit by the riverbank with thy rod; thus shalt thou find peace in his sight.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_3.title: The Voice Between Yawns
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_3.author: Sage Milo
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_3.page_1: Rarely does Belphegor break his slumber to address mortals, for even words feel like a cumbersome burden to him.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_3.page_2: Yet if in thy weariness thou sighest aloud for rest, praisest the sweetness of sleep, or curse arduous toil, thou shalt hear his drowsy voice answer with gentle irony.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_3.page_3: No god understands better the heart of him who only yearns for the serenity of hearth and home.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_4.title: The Mantle of Stillness
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_4.author: Hermit Orin
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_4.page_1: Being now an old man and devout follower of Belphegor, I kept motionless silence before his altar before venturing into dark caverns.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_4.page_2: And his Aura of Stillness walked with me: while my feet advanced without rush or sprint, my wounds knit themselves with gentle soothing.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_4.page_3: And fierce beasts that hurled themselves upon me were overcome by so heavy a slumber that their claws barely managed to graze me.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_5.title: The Punishment of the Striver
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_5.author: Repentant Miner
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_5.page_1: I spent whole days waking, shattering stone with the pickaxe, felling the forest, harvesting fields, and piling stone upon stone without ever touching my bed.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_5.page_2: The more stone I quarried and the more blocks my hands placed without sleeping, the heavier Belphegor's weariness weighed upon me, until his Envoy broke my bones.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_5.page_3: Since that day I seek the rest of my bed before the fatigue of labor accumulates, for only nightly slumber washes away the tally of our toil.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_6.title: Keepers of Slumber
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_6.author: Hermit Orin
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_6.page_1: When I reached the fullness of grace before Belphegor, I did not even have to draw steel when creatures of the night surrounded and wounded me.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_6.page_2: Forthwith two Acolytes in ashen mantles and silent wings descended from the sky, striking down my pursuers while I caught my breath.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_6.page_3: For the Lord of Sloth watches over the sleep of his beloved, that nothing may disturb their rest.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_7.title: The Vigil of the Sleeping Golem
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_7.author: Sage Milo
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_7.page_1: In the villages of Belphegor reigns the most absolute tranquility: none toils, none sows, and green-robed villagers snooze on benches in the sun, delegating all weariness upon the massive shoulders of the great Iron Golem.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_7.page_2: Even when enemy onslaught decimates the village and leaves it desolate, two iron colossi stand dormant vigil guarding the stone of rest, preventing the ungodly from desecrating the sacred bed.
book.sevendeadlygods.sloth_7.page_3: And when assailants seek to wait out the siege while men sleep afar, the battle stands frozen in time: sacred lethargy suspends the count of the siege until the clamor of mortals returns unto the plaza.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_1.title: Song of the Blooming Garden
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_1.author: Poet Julian
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_1.page_1: Asmodeus, Lord of Desire and Beauty, turns his ear away from barren wastelands where dust and naked stone alone reign.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_1.page_2: Adorn therefore the bounds of his altar with fragrant blossoms, amethyst clusters, or music boxes that gladden the air with their notes.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_1.page_3: Offer there purple crystals, honeycombs, or roses, or cause the beasts of the field to join together and bring forth new life beside his sanctuary.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_2.title: The Vestments of Splendor
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_2.author: Royal Goldsmith
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_2.page_1: Present not thyself before the world in crude, graceless iron, for the eyes of Asmodeus take delight in the splendor of forms.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_2.page_2: Take thy cuirass and greaves and adorn them upon the smithing table with filigree and trims of precious metals.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_2.page_3: Whosoever walks adorned in artistry and beauty receives day by day the silent sympathy of the Prince of Desire.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_3.title: Lament of the Withered Meadow
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_3.author: Gardener Clara
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_3.page_1: A boorish man marched into the orchard with his axe, mowing down wild blossoms on a whim, butchering the young of the flock, and putting villagers to the sword.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_3.page_2: The blood on his tool had not yet dried when Asmodeus clouded his vision in thick darkness and cursed him with blazing voice from the heavens.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_3.page_3: Cherish the flower of the field, respect the folk of the villages, and protect the newborn; multiply life upon the earth if thou desirest to find favor before Lust.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_4.title: The Perfume of Grace
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_4.author: Poet Julian
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_4.page_1: Having consecrated my life unto beauty, I celebrated the rite amidst blossoms and melodies, and received upon my brow the Forbidden Charm of Asmodeus.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_4.page_2: A warm balm renewed my vigor at every moment, and as I entered villages and cities, the folk came forth to greet me in wonder, opening their vaults with great generosity.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_4.page_3: For the charm of the Crimson Prince bends wills that no mortal blade could ever subdue.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_5.title: The Thorns of the Rose
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_5.author: Poacher
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_5.page_1: Because I spilled the blood of young woodland calves, wounded peaceful village dwellers, and trampled flowerbeds without mercy, the hatred of Asmodeus fell upon me.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_5.page_2: In the stillness of midnight his Acolytes descended, adorned in amethyst silks and velvet wings, brandishing golden swords sharp as nettle stings.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_5.page_3: I learned with mine own blood that behind the fair countenance of Desire lurks deadly wrath against the destroyers of life.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_6.title: Crimson Epiphany
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_6.author: Lady Seraphina
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_6.page_1: When my soul was attuned unto the designs of Asmodeus, I played sweet melodies beside the flowered altar and offered the purest pearl of the ocean.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_6.page_2: Then a shower of petals and pink embers enveloped the garden, and the Avatar of Lust manifested in all his majesty and beauty.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_6.page_3: He laid into my hands the Crimson Thorn and spoke to me with words so sweet and profound that my heart was captivated forevermore.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_7.title: The Orchard of Rebirth
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_7.author: Poet Julian
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_7.page_1: Villages consecrated unto Asmodeus are intoxicating gardens where cherry blossoms blanket the ground and strains of invisible melodies caress the senses of all who cross their borders.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_7.page_2: There beasts require no shepherd's hand to multiply: the air, heavy with desire, spontaneously quickens life, and herds flourish in joyful dance around the blooming altar.
book.sevendeadlygods.lust_7.page_3: And if death should reap the lives of all their dwellers, Asmodeus's mourning is fleeting as a breath: in merely a single day of vigil the Pilgrim Caravan arrives in haste, repopulating the orchard before the first blossom withers.

altar.sevendeadlygods.desolate_insuffici: «This shrine mourns its fallen in silence. Only a faithful devotee (+30 Favor) may lead its restoration.»
altar.sevendeadlygods.desolate_prompt: «The temple lies desolate. Lay a sacred offering worthy of my cult to instantly summon a new Pilgrim Caravan.»
altar.sevendeadlygods.miracle_restored: «Thy offering hath rekindled my temple's sacred flame! I have summoned my pilgrims to repopulate this holy land!»
altar.sevendeadlygods.avatar_slumber: «The Altar lies cold and dormant. Following the destruction of their earthly Avatar, the presence of %s rests in deep cosmic slumber... No offering shall be heard until their spirit awakens from the void.»
altar.sevendeadlygods.greed.raw_ore: «Darest thou offer me unrefined raw ore? Raw gold is an insult to my altar; smelt it if thou seekest my favor.»
altar.sevendeadlygods.greed.trinkets: «Darest thou bribe me with worthless trinkets? Bring gold, amethysts, emeralds, diamonds, or netherite unto my altar.»
altar.sevendeadlygods.wrath.too_weak: «Thou art far too weak to bleed here. Slay foes beside my altar or return with more blood!»
altar.sevendeadlygods.gluttony.progress: «More! My table hungers still! (%s/3 courses served)»
altar.sevendeadlygods.gluttony.hint: «Bring forth true delicacies (roasted meats, cakes, golden apples, honey) or devour them before my altar.»
altar.sevendeadlygods.pride.low_altitude: «Darest thou worship me in lowland shadows? Erect my altar upon the highest peaks of the world, above the clouds beneath the open sky.»
altar.sevendeadlygods.pride.not_kneeling: «Kneel (Shift) before touching Lucian's altar, insolent mortal!»
altar.sevendeadlygods.pride.offer_accept: «I have received thine offering on high. Now remain kneeling and speak thy praises unto me in chat.»
altar.sevendeadlygods.pride.hint: «Kneel upon the highest peaks, tender a worthy tribute (gold, jewels, trophies), and praise me in chat.»
altar.sevendeadlygods.pride.praise_hint: «Praise me on bended knee (Shift) upon the heights if thou desirest my favor.»
altar.sevendeadlygods.envy.hint: «Bring me the spoils torn from villagers or foreign coffers (emeralds, enchanted books, pearls, relics) to shatter them here.»
altar.sevendeadlygods.sloth.started: «Good... now cease thy movement. Stay completely still beside my altar for 30 seconds and breathe the calm...»
altar.sevendeadlygods.sloth.hint: «Leave wool, a feather, a clock, or fish upon my altar and stay still for 30 seconds doing absolutely nothing.»
altar.sevendeadlygods.lust.cold_environm: «This place is far too cold and bleak. Encircle my altar with at least 3 flowers, amethysts, or note blocks/jukeboxes.»
altar.sevendeadlygods.lust.hint: «Tender me amethysts, rare blossoms, or honeycombs (or breed new life beside my flowered altar).»
